chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Chu Berry's driving style
summary: Collins knew Chu Berry through Roy Eldridge, and contrasts his forceful chordal style with Ben's melodic playing.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Well, Chew, he died -- I think Chew was killed in an automobile accident, wasn't he?

Yeah. But I knew Chew through Roy. Roy left Fletcher to form his own group, and I went with Roy, so consequently Chew would come down and blow with us all the time. You know, all the time. He was very -- I don't know whether you're familiar with this style, but his style was just the opposite of Ben. He was the driver. Chew was a driver, he was a swinger, you know, forceful. Ben was senseless. You know. Well, Ben was definitely a senseless player. He would just tear your heart out. Chew was -- as I said -- a forceful player, and another style he played strictly with the chord. Ben played a melodic style you know. But shortly after that Chew was killed, so I wasn't -- not having been in New York, yet -- see I'm from the midwest as you know, not having been to New York I didn't have the contact with him. Only through Roy, you know. But we played together many times in Chicago at the Three Deuces. You know. Many times.
